## What’s New

This release restores control of an explicitly selected video DreamView center when Govee Community login is unavailable, and prevents temporary cloud failures from deleting Home Assistant One Click discovery.

### Independent Movie DreamView control

- Select your video sync center by its SKU and stable device ID using `video_dreamview_sku` and `video_dreamview_id`.
- A selected cloud-only center such as R2A80 uses the official Platform API with an API key alone. Email/password and Community topology are not required for this path.
- Real LAN devices keep LAN-first control and the existing configured cloud fallback. Generic `dreamViewToggle` capabilities do not classify other lights as video centers.
- ON/OFF values come from the device capability metadata. Logical Platform errors do not update optimistic state.
- The existing DreamView switch identity is retained and its Home Assistant configuration now explicitly declares optimistic state.

### Compatible ON/OFF scenes

- Added configurable replacement commands for `One-Click: Default: Включить DreamView` and `One-Click: Default: Выключить DreamView`.
- The original UUID-v5 discovery identity, bridge device identity, MQTT command topic and payload format are preserved when the exact full scene names match.
- Successfully loaded original One Click actions take priority while IoT is connected. A deduplicated scene-name list avoids duplicate discovery entities.
- Logs distinguish original IoT actions from replacement DreamView commands. Unrelated Night Mode, ScenicView and group actions are not synthesized from a toggle.

### Discovery and availability

- Preserve previous discovery topics during One Click/home-layout errors, including across restarts. A failed or stale lookup is not treated as a confirmed empty scene list.
- Persist only scene names for recovery; no IoT action bodies or credentials are added to the new discovery cache.
- A successful complete synchronization still removes deleted scenes. Interrupted discovery publication aborts cleanup.
- Original One Click availability is tracked separately from the bridge and follows IoT connection/disconnection. Compatibility replacements remain usable through their independent route.
- Serialize full discovery registration and refresh it after topology synchronization.

### Optional home-layout authentication

- Added experimental `one_click_auth: account` and `auto` strategies, with separate response caches and validated application status.
- `community` remains the default. Account-token compatibility with the live Govee endpoint is not assumed or claimed as verified.
- Existing Account login, AWS IoT, physical-device controls, music modes and virtual-control implementations remain supported.

### Setup and validation

For R2A80, configure the API key plus `video_dreamview_sku: R2A80` and the actual `video_dreamview_id` from Platform device metadata. See [DreamView recovery](https://github.com/serjeleone/govee2mqtt/blob/2026-11-17/docs/DREAMVIEW_RECOVERY.md) for all options and legacy-name matching.

Regression coverage includes API-key-only ON/OFF requests against a mock Platform API, nonstandard advertised enum values, wrong-device rejection, logical API failures, discovery preservation and compatible scene identities. The release workflow runs source checks, unit tests, LAN simulator tests and MQTT integration tests before publication, then builds and signs amd64/aarch64 images.

**Live verification still required:** R2A80 OFF behavior, the exact old full scene names/HA registry identities, and experimental Account-token home-layout access. R2A80 ON was confirmed physically in the preceding diagnostics. No cache purge, retained-discovery reset or entity-registry deletion is required.
